analysis:
Examined base_text lines 1-1046 of ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift. The patch's changed ranges (base ~1305-1529, head ~1305-1589) fall outside the supplied units, so only the patch excerpt shows them. It covers a refactor of reclaimableMemoryGb/reclaimableMemoryBytes into a countingRetainedKVSegments variant plus a new evictionCanReach helper, and the excerpt is truncated. I could not see the head or the rest of the diff.

Security-relevant behavior in the visible base code was unchanged: the artifact-identity weight-hash bracketing around container load (lines 543-641), fail-closed reusableSSDWeightHashDecision (137-152), and the cacheEligibleWeightHash gating of the SSD prefix cache (T-041). Also unchanged: GLM ownership and unproven-load retention, and the load-gate and eviction flow.

The visible memory-admission change is availability and accounting logic (eviction feasibility), not authentication, encryption, attestation, or data-exposure logic. It could affect T-028/T-029-style resource exhaustion only if the feasibility estimate were wrong. The excerpt shows conservative handling: the retained-KV credit is used only to decide whether release could make room, and the post-release memory sample is authoritative. I found no concrete regression.

Remaining question: the full head implementation of evictionCanReach, the releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad changes, and the callers in evictUntilAvailable (past line 1046) were not supplied. Any changes there to KV segment release should be checked for cache-data residue or leaked reservations. Given that coverage limit, a deeper check of the memory-reclamation path is warranted.
